newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek shares end up, recoup part of Monday loss.
newsitem.headline: Greek shares end up, recoup part of Monday loss.

text.p: Greek equities reversed course and gained 0.71 percent in moderate turnover, recovering part of their losses in the last two trading days, analysts said.
But they predicted that the market would mark time, awaiting economic policy signals from the new socialist government.

"We witnessed a correction today after two consecutive drops," said Vassilis Kletsas of Telesis Securities. "We expect the bourse to consolidate above 930 points till the government gives clear, solid signals of its future economic policy."
No uptrend can be sustained without cash injections, added Kletsas.
Many analysts and brokers have attributed the recent retreat of the benchmark index to lack of fresh cash inflows.
Yannos Papandoniou was elevated to economic "czar", heading both the national economy and finance ministries when the new cabinet was announced last week.
The Athens general share index closed 0.71 percent, or 6.78 points higher at 960.39 from Monday's 953.61 close after opening at 953.60 points.
Turnover slipped to 7.12 billion drachmas on volume of 3.50 million shares.

Gainers led decliners 105 to 104 with 32 issues unchanged on 241 traded. Banks gained 0.49 percent, industrials rose 1.01 percent and construction firmed 0.23 percent. Small-caps settled with gains of 0.86 percent.
